cover: Israel election deadlock, deadly Spain train disaster, and Fed rate pause
cover_scene: A split composition showing an Israeli voting booth, emergency rescue lights by a damaged train, and a glowing financial trading screen under storm clouds

slides.scene: A blue voting booth bearing the flag of Israel inside a dimly lit polling station with scattered ballot papers
slides.headline: Israel Election Ends in Deadlock as Netanyahu Leads
slides.body: Partial results in Israel's general election show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leading, but falling short of the 61-seat Knesset majority. Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's opposition remains locked in a stalemate, risking further political impasse.

slides.scene: Emergency response vehicles with flashing blue lights beside overturned high-speed train carriages on tracks under a dark twilight sky
slides.headline: Deadly Train Collision in Spain Kills Dozens
slides.body: At least 68 people died and over 100 were injured after two high-speed trains collided south of Madrid in Toledo province. Spanish transport officials attributed the disaster to an unexpected tracking error as rescue operations continue.

slides.scene: A dark central bank press hall featuring microphone stands on a wooden podium before American flags
slides.headline: US Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady
slides.body: The Federal Reserve voted in a split decision to keep benchmark interest rates at 3.75% to 4.00%. Policymakers cited persistent inflation pressures across the U.S. economy while leaving options open for future rate adjustments.

slides.scene: Glowing semiconductor silicon wafers glowing under neon blue lights inside an automated cleanroom factory
slides.headline: SK Hynix Shares Surge After Record Profit
slides.body: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix saw its shares jump over 8% following a record third-quarter operating profit. The surge was driven by massive global demand for high-bandwidth artificial intelligence memory components.

slides.scene: A large international conference hall with African and Russian flags on a wide stage under bright spotlighting
slides.headline: Putin Pitches Russia as African Partner in Moscow
slides.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin told African leaders at the Russia-Africa Summit that Moscow represents their best non-colonial partner, per Al Jazeera. The statement comes as Russia attempts to counter Western influence across the continent.
